q: The main photosynthetic organs are the _____, which have evolved a large surface area to volume ratio.
e: The main photosynthetic organs are the leaves, which have evolved a large surface area to volume ratio. Leaves is the word, not roots or stems.

q: A large surface area to volume ratio means less distance for carbon dioxide to _____ into the leaf.
e: A large surface area to volume ratio means less distance for carbon dioxide to diffuse into the leaf. So we write diffuse. Leave osmose and transport out.

q: In order to obtain the water and mineral salts they needed for nutrition, plants have extensive _____ systems below the ground.
e: In order to obtain the water and mineral salts they needed for nutrition, plants have extensive root systems below the ground. The blank is root. Not shoot or leaf.

q: Water and mineral ions are absorbed by roots and transported through the _____ to other parts of the plant.
e: Water and mineral ions are absorbed by roots and transported through the xylem to other parts of the plant. Xylem is the word, not phloem or cambium.

q: Glucose is needed by all parts of the plant for respiration and for converting to _____ for making cell walls in areas of growth.
e: Glucose is needed by all parts of the plant for respiration and for converting to cellulose for making cell walls in areas of growth. The blank is cellulose. Not starch or sucrose.

q: Glucose can be moved through the phloem as part of the _____ molecule.
e: Glucose can be moved through the phloem as part of the sucrose molecule. So we write sucrose. Leave glucose and fructose out.

q: To move substances to a certain part of the plant for storage, sugars usually change into the form of _____, for storage in a potato tuber.
e: To move substances to a certain part of the plant for storage, sugars usually change into the form of starch, for storage in a potato tuber. The blank is starch. Not cellulose or glycogen.

q: Plants can rely on _____ to supply their cells with oxygen and to remove carbon dioxide because their energy needs are generally small.
e: Plants can rely on diffusion to supply their cells with oxygen and to remove carbon dioxide because their energy needs are generally small. The blank is diffusion. Not osmosis or active transport.

q: Xylem tissue contains dead, empty hollow cells with no end walls, which are composed of _____ arranged in long lines.
e: Xylem tissue contains dead, empty hollow cells with no end walls, which are composed of xylem vessels arranged in long lines. The blank is xylem vessels. Not sieve tubes or companion cells.

q: Water moves through long, hollow tubes of xylem by _____ from the roots to all other parts of the plant.
e: Water moves through long, hollow tubes of xylem by mass flow from the roots to all other parts of the plant. The blank is mass flow. Not diffusion or osmosis.

q: Phloem tissue contains cells called _____ which are living cells and contain cytoplasm and a few organelles but no nucleus.
e: Phloem tissue contains cells called sieve tube which are living cells and contain cytoplasm and a few organelles but no nucleus. The blank is sieve tube. Not companion cell or tracheid.

q: A _____ cell is associated with each sieve tube in the phloem tissue.
e: A companion cell is associated with each sieve tube in the phloem tissue. The blank is companion. Not parenchyma or epidermal.

q: The walls of sieve tubes in the phloem tissue are made of _____.
e: The walls of sieve tubes in the phloem tissue are made of cellulose. So we write cellulose. Leave suberin and lignin out.

q: The plant body spreads out to obtain carbon dioxide, light energy, water and inorganic mineral ions to make organic molecules like sugars and _____.
e: The plant body spreads out to obtain carbon dioxide, light energy, water and inorganic mineral ions to make organic molecules like sugars and amino acids. So we write amino acids. Leave fatty acids and nucleic acids out.

q: Plants have two transport systems: xylem and _____.
e: Plants have two transport systems: xylem and phloem. The blank is phloem. Not cambium or epidermis.

q: Within a plant, mineral ions and organic compounds are transported by being dissolved in _____.
e: Within a plant, mineral ions and organic compounds are transported by being dissolved in water. So we write water. Leave minerals and sucrose out.

q: The uptake of water by plant roots is a passive process and occurs by _____.
e: The uptake of water by plant roots is a passive process and occurs by osmosis. Osmosis is the word, not active transport or diffusion.

q: In active absorption, the movement where protoplasm is involved is called _____.
e: In active absorption, the movement where protoplasm is involved is called symplast. So we write symplast. Leave apoplast and xylem out.

q: In passive absorption, water moves through the _____ of the root, which includes the cell wall and intercellular spaces.
e: In passive absorption, water moves through the apoplast of the root, which includes the cell wall and intercellular spaces. The blank is apoplast. Not phloem or symplast.

q: Most water travels via the apoplastic pathway through the hollow tubes of the _____.
e: Most water travels via the apoplastic pathway through the hollow tubes of the xylem. Xylem is the word, not phloem or cambium.

q: The water moves by _____ in the apoplastic pathway as it does not pass through a partially permeable membrane.
e: The water moves by diffusion in the apoplastic pathway as it does not pass through a partially permeable membrane. The blank is diffusion. Not osmosis or active transport.

q: When water reaches the endodermis, a thick, waterproof, waxy band of _____ within the cell wall blocks the apoplastic pathway.
e: When water reaches the endodermis, a thick, waterproof, waxy band of suberin within the cell wall blocks the apoplastic pathway. So we write suberin. Leave lignin and cutin out.

q: The band that forms an impassable barrier for water in the endodermis is called the _____.
e: The band that forms an impassable barrier for water in the endodermis is called the Casparian strip. The blank is Casparian strip. Not endodermis or pericycle.

q: A smaller amount of water travels via the symplastic pathway, which is the cytoplasm and _____ or vacuole of the cells.
e: A smaller amount of water travels via the symplastic pathway, which is the cytoplasm and plasmodesmata or vacuole of the cells. So we write plasmodesmata. Leave tonoplast and cell membrane out.

q: The movement of water in the symplastic pathway is _____ than the apoplastic pathway.
e: The movement of water in the symplastic pathway is slower than the apoplastic pathway. Slower is the word, not faster or equal.

q: The uptake of minerals by plant roots can be passive transport and/or _____ transport.
e: The uptake of minerals by plant roots can be passive transport and/or active transport. So we write active. Leave passive and facilitated out.

q: Plant roots can have _____ to increase the surface area for absorption of water and mineral ions.
e: Plant roots can have root hairs to increase the surface area for absorption of water and mineral ions. So we write root hairs. Leave stomata and lenticels out.

q: In the symplastic pathway, water moves into the vacuole through the _____ by osmosis.
e: In the symplastic pathway, water moves into the vacuole through the tonoplast by osmosis. The blank is tonoplast. Not plasma membrane or cell wall.

q: Two pathways that initiate the passage of water from root hair to xylem are apoplastic and _____.
e: Two pathways that initiate the passage of water from root hair to xylem are apoplastic and symplastic. The blank is symplastic. Not transmembrane or vascular.

q: The apoplastic and symplastic routes may exist simultaneously or separately having different _____.
e: The apoplastic and symplastic routes may exist simultaneously or separately having different rates. So we write rates. Leave volumes and pressures out.

q: The cells in the mesophyll layers are not tightly packed and have many spaces around them filled with _____.
e: The cells in the mesophyll layers are not tightly packed and have many spaces around them filled with air. So we write air. Leave water and sap out.

q: The air inside the leaf contacts the outside air through small pores called _____.
e: The air inside the leaf contacts the outside air through small pores called stomata. Stomata is the word, not lenticels or pores.

q: Water vapour diffuses out of the leaf down a water potential gradient by the process of _____.
e: Water vapour diffuses out of the leaf down a water potential gradient by the process of transpiration. So we write transpiration. Leave osmosis and diffusion out.

q: In condition of low humidity, the gradient is steep, so transpiration takes place more _____.
e: In condition of low humidity, the gradient is steep, so transpiration takes place more quickly. The blank is quickly. Not slowly or equally.

q: Transpiration rate may be increased by an increase in _____ or rising in temperature.
e: Transpiration rate may be increased by an increase in wind speed or rising in temperature. The blank is wind speed. Not light intensity or soil moisture.

q: Stomata close at night, so the rate of transpiration is almost _____ at night.
e: Stomata close at night, so the rate of transpiration is almost zero at night. Zero is the word, not maximum or minimum.

q: In especially dry conditions, a plant may compromise by partially or completely closing its _____ to prevent leaves drying out.
e: In especially dry conditions, a plant may compromise by partially or completely closing its stomata to prevent leaves drying out. Stomata is the word, not roots or leaves.

q: As water evaporates from cell walls inside the leaf, it absorbs _____ from these cells, reducing their temperature.
e: As water evaporates from cell walls inside the leaf, it absorbs heat energy from these cells, reducing their temperature. So we write heat energy. Leave light energy and chemical energy out.

q: If water loss exceeds uptake, cells become less turgid and the plant _____ as soft parts lose support.
e: If water loss exceeds uptake, cells become less turgid and the plant wilts as soft parts lose support. The blank is wilts. Not grows or dies.

q: Ascent of sap mostly occurs due to _____ exerted by transpiration of water.
e: Ascent of sap mostly occurs due to transpiration pull exerted by transpiration of water. So we write transpiration pull. Leave root pressure and osmotic pressure out.

q: Transpiration lowers the temperature of plants by 10°-_____ °C by evaporating water.
e: Transpiration lowers the temperature of plants by 10°-15 °C by evaporating water. The blank is 15. Not 10 or 20.

q: The development of _____ tissue, essential for rigidity and strength, is favoured by an increase in transpiration.
e: The development of mechanical tissue, essential for rigidity and strength, is favoured by an increase in transpiration. Mechanical is the word, not vascular or epidermal.

q: The loss of water through transpiration _____ the concentration of mineral salts in the plant.
e: The loss of water through transpiration increases the concentration of mineral salts in the plant. Increases is the word, not decreases or maintains.

q: The ash and _____ content of the fruit increases with the increase in transpiration.
e: The ash and sugar content of the fruit increases with the increase in transpiration. So we write sugar. Leave starch and protein out.

q: Excessive transpiration induces hardening and resistance to moderate _____.
e: Excessive transpiration induces hardening and resistance to moderate drought. Drought is the word, not cold or heat.

q: Transpiration results in pulling of water, molecule by molecule into the leaf from the _____.
e: Transpiration results in pulling of water, molecule by molecule into the leaf from the xylem. The blank is xylem. Not phloem or roots.

q: In the demonstration of transpiration pull, the bottom of the thistle funnel is immersed in a bowl of _____.
e: In the demonstration of transpiration pull, the bottom of the thistle funnel is immersed in a bowl of mercury. So we write mercury. Leave water and oil out.

q: Loss of water from the twig produces a _____ in the thistle funnel and water will be drawn up.
e: Loss of water from the twig produces a vacuum in the thistle funnel and water will be drawn up. So we write vacuum. Leave pressure and gas out.

q: Stomata must be opened during the day to allow _____ to diffuse into the leaf for photosynthesis.
e: Stomata must be opened during the day to allow carbon dioxide to diffuse into the leaf for photosynthesis. So we write carbon dioxide. Leave oxygen and nitrogen out.

q: Transpiration helps the shape and structure of plant parts by keeping cells _____.
e: Transpiration helps the shape and structure of plant parts by keeping cells turgid. Turgid is the word, not flaccid or plasmolysed.

q: Translocation is the movement of _____ substances through a plant.
e: Translocation is the movement of dissolved substances through a plant. The blank is dissolved. Not solid or gaseous.

q: Food synthesized in leaves passes downwards or upwards in the _____ tubes of the phloem.
e: Food synthesized in leaves passes downwards or upwards in the sieve tubes of the phloem. So we write sieve. Leave xylem and tracheid out.

q: Carbohydrates produced by leaves are transported out of the leaf in the form of _____ to the stem.
e: Carbohydrates produced by leaves are transported out of the leaf in the form of sucrose to the stem. So we write sucrose. Leave glucose and starch out.

q: Sucrose may travel downwards to the roots and underground _____ organs.
e: Sucrose may travel downwards to the roots and underground storage organs. Storage is the word, not reproductive or photosynthetic.

q: Both upward and downward movement of substances may take place at the _____ time in the phloem.
e: Both upward and downward movement of substances may take place at the same time in the phloem. So we write same. Leave different and opposite out.

q: Phloem tissue components are sieve tube, companion cell, phloem parenchyma and phloem _____.
e: Phloem tissue components are sieve tube, companion cell, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibre. So we write fibre. Leave vessel and tracheid out.

q: In translocation, sieve tubes which have no nucleus and _____ cells work together.
e: In translocation, sieve tubes which have no nucleus and companion cells work together. Companion is the word, not parenchyma or epidermal.

q: Perforations in the cell septate walls of sieve cells are known as sieve _____.
e: Perforations in the cell septate walls of sieve cells are known as sieve plates. Plates is the word, not pores or membranes.

q: Sieve cells are kept alive by nucleated _____ cells situated adjacent to them.
e: Sieve cells are kept alive by nucleated companion cells situated adjacent to them. Companion is the word, not parenchyma or xylem.

q: There are profuse _____ connections between sieve and companion cells.
e: There are profuse cytoplasmic connections between sieve and companion cells. Cytoplasmic is the word, not vascular or nuclear.

q: Large multicellular animals have evolved transport systems as they get larger and have higher _____ rates.
e: Large multicellular animals have evolved transport systems as they get larger and have higher metabolic rates. Metabolic is the word, not reproductive or growth.

q: In many large animals, including vertebrates, the circulatory system is in the form of a _____ transport system.
e: In many large animals, including vertebrates, the circulatory system is in the form of a mass transport system. The blank is mass. Not simple or passive.

q: Single-celled organisms have a _____ surface area to volume ratio.
e: Single-celled organisms have a high surface area to volume ratio. So we write high. Leave low and equal out.

q: In large multicellular organisms, the surface area to volume ratio is _____.
e: In large multicellular organisms, the surface area to volume ratio is low. Low is the word, not high or equal.

q: Respiration supplies energy but also produces the toxic waste product _____.
e: Respiration supplies energy but also produces the toxic waste product carbon dioxide. The blank is carbon dioxide. Not oxygen or glucose.

q: Mass transport systems have exchange surfaces and a system of _____ that carry substances.
e: Mass transport systems have exchange surfaces and a system of vessels that carry substances. Vessels is the word, not cells or organs.

q: Moving materials fast may involve mechanical methods such as the pumping of the _____.
e: Moving materials fast may involve mechanical methods such as the pumping of the heart. The blank is heart. Not lungs or kidneys.

q: Mass transport systems require a suitable transport medium, which is usually a _____.
e: Mass transport systems require a suitable transport medium, which is usually a fluid. The blank is fluid. Not gas or solid.

q: Cells require a supply of chemical substances such as glucose and _____ for cellular respiration.
e: Cells require a supply of chemical substances such as glucose and oxygen for cellular respiration. Oxygen is the word, not water or carbon.

q: Most mass transport systems adapt the rate of transport to the _____ of the organism.
e: Most mass transport systems adapt the rate of transport to the needs of the organism. The blank is needs. Not size or shape.

q: In an open circulatory system, blood leaves vessels to a series of blood _____ surrounding tissues.
e: In an open circulatory system, blood leaves vessels to a series of blood spaces surrounding tissues. So we write spaces. Leave vessels and veins out.

q: When the insect heart relaxes, blood flows back into vessels through pores called _____.
e: When the insect heart relaxes, blood flows back into vessels through pores called ostia. The blank is ostia. Not valves or pores.

q: Open circulatory system is found in most _____, such as insects, spiders and crabs.
e: Open circulatory system is found in most arthropods, such as insects, spiders and crabs. So we write arthropods. Leave vertebrates and molluscs out.

q: In a closed system, blood vessels carry blood to the _____ of the entire body.
e: In a closed system, blood vessels carry blood to the tissues of the entire body. Tissues is the word, not cells or organs.

q: Closed systems direct flow precisely to organs that need most oxygen and _____.
e: Closed systems direct flow precisely to organs that need most oxygen and nutrients. So we write nutrients. Leave water and hormones out.

q: In fish, the heart pumps deoxygenated blood to the _____, the organs of gas exchange.
e: In fish, the heart pumps deoxygenated blood to the gills, the organs of gas exchange. So we write gills. Leave lungs and skin out.

q: In a single circulatory system, blood passes _____ through the heart for each complete circuit.
e: In a single circulatory system, blood passes once through the heart for each complete circuit. Once is the word, not twice or thrice.

q: Birds and mammals have a double circulatory system involving systemic and _____ circulations.
e: Birds and mammals have a double circulatory system involving systemic and pulmonary circulations. So we write pulmonary. Leave systemic and coronary out.

q: Systemic circulation carries _____ blood from the heart to the body cells.
e: Systemic circulation carries oxygenated blood from the heart to the body cells. Oxygenated is the word, not deoxygenated or mixed.

q: Pulmonary circulation carries oxygenated blood back to the _____.
e: Pulmonary circulation carries oxygenated blood back to the heart. Heart is the word, not lungs or brain.

q: In a double circulatory system, blood passes _____ through the heart for each complete circuit.
e: In a double circulatory system, blood passes twice through the heart for each complete circuit. So we write twice. Leave once and thrice out.

q: Birds and mammals need much oxygen because they maintain a constant body _____.
e: Birds and mammals need much oxygen because they maintain a constant body temperature. So we write temperature. Leave pressure and volume out.

q: Separate circuits in double circulation ensure oxygenated and deoxygenated blood cannot _____.
e: Separate circuits in double circulation ensure oxygenated and deoxygenated blood cannot separate. So we write separate. Leave mix and clot out.

q: Blood going through tiny vessels in the lungs is at relatively _____ pressure to prevent damage.
e: Blood going through tiny vessels in the lungs is at relatively low pressure to prevent damage. Low is the word, not high or variable.

q: Oxygenated blood returning to the heart is pumped around the body at _____ pressure.
e: Oxygenated blood returning to the heart is pumped around the body at high pressure. So we write high. Leave low and zero out.

q: The upper two chambers of the human heart are the right atrium and the left _____.
e: The upper two chambers of the human heart are the right atrium and the left right atrium. Right atrium is the word, not left atrium or left ventricle.

q: The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the superior and _____ vena cava.
e: The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the superior and inferior vena cava. The blank is inferior. Not superior or pulmonary.

q: The left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the lungs via _____ veins.
e: The left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the lungs via pulmonary veins. The blank is pulmonary. Not coronary or systemic.

q: Deoxygenated blood in the right ventricle enters the lungs through the pulmonary _____.
e: Deoxygenated blood in the right ventricle enters the lungs through the pulmonary artery. The blank is artery. Not vein or capillary.

q: The two sides of the heart are separated by a complete thick, muscular _____.
e: The two sides of the heart are separated by a complete thick, muscular septum. The blank is septum. Not valve or wall.

q: Cardiac muscle has a good blood supply by the _____ arteries.
e: Cardiac muscle has a good blood supply by the coronary arteries. Coronary is the word, not pulmonary or systemic.

q: Cardiac muscle contains lots of _____, a respiratory pigment with strong affinity for oxygen.
e: Cardiac muscle contains lots of myoglobin, a respiratory pigment with strong affinity for oxygen. The blank is myoglobin. Not haemoglobin or chlorophyll.

q: The muscular wall of the left ventricle is much _____ than that of the right ventricle.
e: The muscular wall of the left ventricle is much thicker than that of the right ventricle. The blank is thicker. Not thinner or equal.

q: The right atrioventricular valve is called the _____ valve.
e: The right atrioventricular valve is called the tricuspid valve. So we write tricuspid. Leave bicuspid and semilunar out.

q: The left atrioventricular valve is called bicuspid or _____ valve.
e: The left atrioventricular valve is called bicuspid or tricuspid valve. So we write tricuspid. Leave mitral and pulmonary out.

q: Flaps of AV valves are supported by the cordae tendineae, also known as _____.
e: Flaps of AV valves are supported by the cordae tendineae, also known as valves. Valves is the word, not tendinous cords or septum.

q: Semilunar valves are located at the base of the pulmonary artery and the _____.
e: Semilunar valves are located at the base of the pulmonary artery and the aorta. Aorta is the word, not vein or vena cava.

q: Arteries carrying deoxygenated blood include the pulmonary artery and the _____ artery.
e: Arteries carrying deoxygenated blood include the pulmonary artery and the coronary artery. Coronary is the word, not umbilical or carotid.

q: The very smallest branches of the arterial system, furthest from the heart, are the _____.
e: The very smallest branches of the arterial system, furthest from the heart, are the arterioles. So we write arterioles. Leave venules and capillaries out.

q: Elastic fibers in artery walls return to original length to maintain pressure, which is called _____.
e: Elastic fibers in artery walls return to original length to maintain pressure, which is called recoil. The blank is recoil. Not contraction or expansion.

q: Between the capillaries and the cells is a watery liquid called _____ fluid.
e: Between the capillaries and the cells is a watery liquid called tissue fluid. The blank is tissue. Not interstitial or plasma.

q: Most of the water from tissue fluid reenters capillaries by _____.
e: Most of the water from tissue fluid reenters capillaries by osmosis. So we write osmosis. Leave diffusion and active transport out.

q: The lymphatic system consists of vessels similar to blood _____.
e: The lymphatic system consists of vessels similar to blood capillaries. So we write capillaries. Leave arteries and veins out.

q: The lymphatic system transports the fluid, called _____, back to the blood.
e: The lymphatic system transports the fluid, called lymph, back to the blood. The blank is lymph. Not plasma or serum.

q: Lymph returns to the blood by opening into the _____ veins.
e: Lymph returns to the blood by opening into the subclavian veins. So we write subclavian. Leave jugular and femoral out.

q: The _____ that carry fats from villi of the small intestine are part of the lymphatic system.
e: The lacteals that carry fats from villi of the small intestine are part of the lymphatic system. So we write lacteals. Leave capillaries and venules out.

q: Before lymph passes back into the blood, it is filtered to remove dead cells and bacteria in swellings called lymph _____.
e: Before lymph passes back into the blood, it is filtered to remove dead cells and bacteria in swellings called lymph nodes. Nodes is the word, not vessels or ducts.

q: Lymph nodes contain _____ blood cells that are important in destroying harmful bacteria.
e: Lymph nodes contain white blood cells that are important in destroying harmful bacteria. White is the word, not red or platelet.

q: When a person gets an infection, one of the first signs may be swelling of the lymph nodes, often referred to as swollen _____.
e: When a person gets an infection, one of the first signs may be swelling of the lymph nodes, often referred to as swollen glands. Glands is the word, not tissues or organs.
